title: Synthesizing Past Modals in Bioethical Argumentation

sections.title: The Three Pillars of Ethical Evaluation
sections.content: When evaluating a complex medical or moral case at B2, combine all three past modal perspectives: (1) Epistemic foreseeability ('Mit tudhatott volna az orvos?' — What could the doctor have known?), (2) Potential prevention ('Mit lehetett volna megelőzni?' — What could have been prevented?), and (3) Deontic duty ('Mit kellett volna tennie?' — What should he/she have done?).

sections.title: Németh László's Moral Psychology
sections.content: In Iszony, László Németh—himself a practicing physician—uses past modals to probe the boundary between external duty and inner conscience. Even when an objective observer concludes 'ennél többet senki sem tehetett volna' (nobody could have done more), the protagonist's conscience still asks 'másképp kellett volna éreznem' (I should have felt differently).

sections.title: Comprehensive Past Modal Matrix
rows: Megelőzhette volna / El lehetett volna kerülni (Could have prevented/avoided)
Intézkednie kellett volna (Should have taken action)
Nem szabadott volna halogatni (Should not have postponed)

items.spanish: Bár a szövődményt senki sem láthatta előre, a beteget korábban kórházba kellett volna szállítani.
items.english: Although nobody could have foreseen the complication, the patient should have been taken to hospital earlier.

items.spanish: Ha időben felismerik a tüneteket, el lehetett volna kerülni a tragédiát.
items.english: Had they recognized the symptoms in time, the tragedy could have been avoided.

items.spanish: Az ápolónőnek nem volt miért vádolnia magát: ennél odaadóbban senki sem virraszthatott volna.
items.english: The nurse had no reason to blame herself: nobody could have kept vigil more devotedly than this.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: Use concessive framing ('Bár senki sem láthatta előre..., mégis óvatosabbnak kellett volna lenni') to construct balanced, high-scoring B2 argumentative essays.
